title: Benefit concert and Lee's death
summary: With money gone, musicians organized a suburban Chicago benefit; Lee kept declining and died after leaving hospital for home.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: we were spending. Whatever money you had.
What we had was really gone. So, they decided to give her a benefit.
Who played, who showed for the benefit?

Oh, my goodness. I'm going to get to that. But the benefit was supposed to be given at the Blue Note. Louis Armstrong and Gary Crosby were there in Chicago, Chicago Theater. And something, some reason, I don't know who did it, but they canceled it. So, the musician decided not to give it in Chicago, decided to give it out in the suburbs. They did. So, the Dukes of Dixieland came. And musicians from England, oh, several bands came. And they played for this benefit, which was quite successful. You couldn't get in the hall. And that's how that benefit ended up. But Lee never got well after this episode. He was in and out of the hospital quite often. And so, he was still discouraged. And then I had to watch him when he got home because the doctor said he may, you know, attempt it again. But he didn't. He just gave up and he refused to see his friends. And they had the Barno's from Belgium came to see him. And he liked them very much when we were in Europe. And he would not let me put the light on to see, you know, he was wasting away. And so, but on the last go-round, just three days before his death, he asked me to take him out of the hospital. And I did. I brought him home. And he was very happy. But that was it, you know.
Then he died. Right. Right then.
